name: Rosemary
imageAlt: fresh vibrant green aromatic rosemary sprigs with needle-like leaves, releasing concentrated essential oils from their woody stems
description: Rosemary (Salvia rosmarinus) is a dense, aromatic perennial woody herb belonging to the mint family, presenting a highly concentrated, bioactively potent phytochemical matrix optimized for neurological protection, micro-vascular defense, and profound systemic antioxidant mitigation. The primary therapeutic architecture of rosemary relies on its unique yield of terpene and phenolic derivatives—principally rosmarinic acid, carnosic acid, and carnosol—alongside volatile essential monoterpenes (1,8-cineole and camphor). Operating within human metabolic environments, these secondary plant metabolites directly block lipid peroxidation cascades, suppress systemic inflammatory markers, and optimize acetylcholinesterase balance to support clear cognitive pathway dynamics.
macroIntro: Rosemary possesses a highly concentrated, non-hydrating macro architecture rich in structural dietary fibers, volatile lipid elements, and foundational mineral complexes.
microIntro: The needle-like leaves pack an extraordinary payload of neuroprotective organic acids, strong free-radical scavenging polyphenols, and skeletal-reinforcing mineral salts.

healthBenefits: Neuroprotective Cognitive Support: Active carnosic acid and 1,8-cineole cross directly into neural networks, shielding brain tissue from oxidative atrophy and boosting memory focus metrics.

precautionsIntro: Uterine Contraction Triggers, Camphor-Driven Neuroexcitability, and Severe Ephedrine-Like Drug Interferences: Advanced clinical application mandates strict safety boundaries.
precautions: Uterine Stimulation and Emmenagogue Risks: Rosemary contains highly concentrated volatile fractions that act as potent emmenagogues. In pregnant individuals, medicinal or excessive amounts can trigger unwanted uterine contractions, pelvic blood flow surge, and potential pregnancy termination.

Neurological Toxicity and Camphor Overload: The essential oils within rosemary leaves store noticeable amounts of camphor. Ingesting concentrated rosemary oil or raw extracts in massive volumes can induce central nervous system overstimulation, leading to severe dizziness, vomiting, or grand mal seizures.

Gastrointestinal Mucosal Inflammation and Bleeding: Due to the high density of volatile terpenes and tough structural fibers, consuming excessive raw rosemary stalks can cause direct mucosal irritation, severe abdominal cramping, and potential kidney irritation from hyper-clearance pathways.
